title: Velvety Crumbly Polish Potato Pancakes
description: A traditional Polish dish featuring garlicky and crumbly potato pancakes, made with soda water for a light and fluffy texture, and namul-blanch-season method for added flavor.
instructions: In a large bowl, combine grated potatoes, onion, and garlic, and squeeze out as much moisture as possible using a cheesecloth or a clean dish towel.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, egg, salt, and pepper, and add the soda water, stirring until smooth.
Add the dry ingredients to the potato mixture, and stir until just combined, being careful not to overmix.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat, and using a 1/4 cup measuring cup, scoop the potato mixture into the skillet, flattening slightly with a spatula.
Cook the pancakes for 4-5 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crispy, adjusting the heat as needed to prevent burning.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the pancakes from the oil, and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the pancakes hot, garnished with chopped fresh parsley or chives, and accompanied by a dollop of sour cream or applesauce, if desired.
Repeat the cooking process with the remaining potato mixture, adjusting the heat as needed to prevent burning.
